Under $72 a cell is a height; $72 to $7E are special ground with routines of their own ($9267). Unpacked from the area's record by $87CF; zeros at the hand-over.

Four bytes for each area: the address of its packed ground, then two offsets written into $90DE ($90E2, $90F0) and $9230 ($9237, $9244), across and down, added to a place before its cell is found. Areas 0 and 1 share their ground. The entry for area 15 would be the first four bytes of the packed data at $D03C, and so an address of $00FF; no route, record or object is in area 15.

Area 0 and 1's ground, packed: a byte with bit 7 set is a count (its low seven bits) and the next byte is repeated that many times; any other byte is one cell. $87CF unpacks it until bank 1's $D000 is reached, so a last run may end part-way and the next area's data can begin inside it.

Which animation an actor plays, read by $8FDA when its action (+$0C) changes: twelve bytes for each of 24 values of its animation state (+$0D), one for each action. The byte is the animation's number in the actor's list (bit 7 to play it backwards from its last frame); the byte two after it (one after, played backwards), unless $FF, becomes the actor's new state.
The animations of types $14 to $17 (actor class 6, bank 3's $EAC8): 24 words, each the address of a script.
The animations of type $2D (class 11): 9 scripts.
The animations of the four characters and most other types (classes 0 to 4 and 7 to 10): 62 scripts, numbers 0 to 61.
The animations of types $10 to $13 (class 5): 24 scripts, several shared with the list at $E454.

The animation scripts, 85 of them to $E95F: a count of frames n, three bytes (the fourth, at +3, names in its high nibble the event at the animation's end, $9052, $F for none), then n frames of four bytes: the moves across, down and in height, signed, and the sprite frame shown (+$1B, bit 7 mirrored), whose low nibble is also the leader's scroll step ($98FF). The scripts at $E628, $E650 and $E784 to $E79C are in none of the four lists.
Animation scripts, continued: the first four, $E784 to $E79F, are in none of the four lists.

136 bytes between Dirk's pictures that none of bank 1's frame lists names.

The pictures of type $2D, then its two masks ($FF75, $FFBD). The mask at $FFBD is 69 bytes by its frame's size and would run past $FFFF.
